overview.title: Process overview
overview.description: What this invoice is, where it is, and the data behind every step.
overview.introLead: Store-Pit buys parcels in bulk from GLS
overview.introBody: and re-bills them to each of its clients with a margin. This screen follows one weekly GLS invoice through the eight steps that turn a single mixed bill into a clean, per-client settlement. Click any step to open the data behind it.

steps.sourceFiles: GLS sends two files each week - a CSV with every parcel and a PDF with the rate summary. Everything starts here.
steps.extraction: Read those files into clean shipment lines. This is the only step that is OCR - everything after it is calculation.
steps.reconciliation: Check the numbers tie out: the CSV total equals the PDF total and parcel counts match. Bad data is caught before any billing.
steps.classification: Work out which client each parcel belongs to, from the reference code on it (FP- is FlatPay, NV is Nordvio, and so on).
steps.netting: Match GLS discounts to the right parcels and subtract them first, so the saving is passed to the client before any margin.
steps.reRating: Apply each client's own price deal - FlatPay x1.1, Braintimizer's contract, Drywear and Nordvio off a price list. This is the heart of it, not a flat markup.
steps.aggregation: Roll everything up per client and country, then add the surcharges - energy, road tolls and pre-financing.
steps.export: Each client gets a clean statement: their parcels, their countries, the amount to settle. Store-Pit sees its margin.
